name: dither-field
title: Dither Field
description: A full-bleed background of purple light rendered as crisp square dots, glowing like a horizon and blooming around the mouse. It can also dither an image or video, and it holds overlaid page content.
use: A landing page wants a rich animated backdrop that feels technical and reacts to the cursor without heavy artwork.
avoid: It needs WebGL2 and a sized parent, falls back to a static CSS dot pattern on old devices, and never fully settles.
a11y: The dot canvas is aria-hidden and decorative; it pauses under reduced motion or a hidden tab, needing WebGL2 or a CSS dot fallback. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A full-width dark stage washed in purple light that reads as a horizon glow, brightening to near-white near the bottom centre. The surface is built from tiny square dithered dots rather than smooth gradients, densest where the light is brightest, with a loose band of haze across the middle.
behaves: The glow drifts and flickers slowly on its own and brightens strongly around the mouse, pen or a held finger, easing back after the pointer. It pauses when scrolled out of view or when the tab is hidden; the demo centres a headline, paragraph and two buttons over it.
customise: Pattern, image or video src, colour ramp, dot size, intensity, speed, fps and interactive are props; custom patterns and the shaders need source edits. Children sit above the dots.
weight: heavy: A WebGL2 shader loop runs every frame and rebuilds mipmaps; it pauses off-screen or on a hidden tab.
